literal: Juqu Mengxun sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun sent envoys with tribute.

literal: On renyin Marquis of Shouguang Shusun Jian was enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang.
idiomatic: On renyin Shusun Jian, Marquis of Shouguang, was made Prince of Danyang.

literal: Twelfth month, day dingmao: Ding's younger brothers Sheyu and Duluo Gugu came bound in surrender; Pingliang was pacified and their treasures were seized.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingmao, Ding's brothers Sheyu and Duluo Gugu surrendered bound; Pingliang fell and their treasures were taken.

literal: The garrison commanders of Chang'an, Linjin, and Wugong all fled; Guanzhong was pacified.
idiomatic: The defenders of Chang'an, Linjin, and Wugong all fled; Guanzhong was pacified.

literal: On renshen the imperial carriage returned east, leaving Duke of Badong Yanpu and others to garrison Anding.
idiomatic: On renshen the court turned east, leaving Yanpu, Duke of Badong, and others to hold Anding.

literal: That year Feng Ba died and his brother Wentong seized the throne.
idiomatic: That year Feng Ba died and his brother Wentong usurped rule.

literal: Year 4, spring, first month, day renwu: the imperial carriage halted at Mugen Mountain, held a great feast for the ministers, and distributed cloth and silk, each according to rank.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, first month of spring, on renwu the court halted at Mugen Mountain, feasted the ministers, and gave cloth and silk by rank.

literal: On bingshen Liu Yilong's generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde came from Qingshui to relieve Huatai; Prince of Danyang Shusun Jian and Duke of Yiyin Changsun Daosheng barred them, and Daoji and the others did not dare advance.
idiomatic: On bingshen Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde of Liu Yilong came from Qingshui to save Huatai; Shusun Jian, Prince of Danyang, and Changsun Daosheng, Duke of Yiyin, blocked them and they did not advance.

literal: That month Qifu Mumo was destroyed by Helian Ding.
idiomatic: That month Qifu Mumo was destroyed by Helian Ding.

literal: Second month, day xinyou: An Gu and Sima Chuzhi pacified Huatai and captured Yilong's generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande and Administrator of Dongjun Shen Mo.
idiomatic: On xinyou of the second month An Gu and Sima Chuzhi took Huatai and captured Zhu Xiuzhi, Li Yuande, and Shen Mo, governor of Dongjun.

literal: On guiyou the imperial carriage returned to the palace, held a feast celebrating merit, reported at the ancestral temple, rewarded the capital officials each according to rank, and granted soldiers ten years' tax exemption.
idiomatic: On guiyou the court returned to the capital, feasted the victors, reported to the ancestral temple, rewarded the capital officials, and exempted soldiers from levies for ten years.

literal: On dingchou he traveled to the Southern Palace.
idiomatic: On dingchou he went to the Southern Palace.

literal: The people of Ding province were hungry; an edict opened the granaries for relief.
idiomatic: Ding province was in famine; granaries were opened for relief.

literal: Yilong's generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde fled east; the generals pursued them to Licheng and returned.
idiomatic: Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde fled east; pursuers reached Licheng and turned back.

literal: Third month, day gengxu: Champion General An Gu presented more than ten thousand of Yilong's captives and thirty thousand suits of armor.
idiomatic: On gengxu of the third month An Gu, Champion General, presented more than ten thousand captives and thirty thousand suits of armor.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day gengyin: traveled to Yunzhong.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on gengyin, he went to Yunzhong.

literal: Sixth month: Helian Ding raided north against Juqu Mengxun and was seized by Murong Mugui of Tuyuhun.
idiomatic: In the sixth month Helian Ding raided Juqu Mengxun in the north and was captured by Murong Mugui of Tuyuhun.

literal: Intercalary month, day yimao: the Rouran state sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on yimao, the Rouran sent tribute.

literal: An edict that Attendant Cadet Zhou Shao was envoy to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: He ordered Attendant Cadet Zhou Shao to Liu Yilong as envoy.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jiyou: traveled to Hexi and began the Chenghua Palace.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiyou, he went to Hexi and began Chenghua Palace.

literal: Eighth month, day yiyou: Juqu Mengxun sent his son Anzhou to attend court.
idiomatic: On yiyou of the eighth month Juqu Mengxun sent his son Anzhou to court.

literal: Murong Mugui of Tuyuhun sent envoys with a memorial requesting to hand over Helian Ding.
idiomatic: Murong Mugui sent envoys asking to deliver Helian Ding.

literal: On jichou Mugui was made Grand General and King of Western Qin.
idiomatic: On jichou Mugui was made Grand General and King of Western Qin.

literal: Ninth month, day guichou: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guichou, the court returned to the capital.

literal: On gengshen Grand Tutor Changsun Song was given the additional title Grand General with Pillar of State; Cui Hao, Special Advance and Left Grand Master of the Palace, was made Chancellor; Changsun Daosheng, General Who Conquers the West, was made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: On gengshen Changsun Song, Grand Tutor, received the added rank Grand General with Pillar of State; Cui Hao became Chancellor; Changsun Daosheng, General Who Conquers the West, became Minister of Works.

literal: On renhai an edict that Concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies Li Shun, bearing credentials, was to invest Juqu Mengxun, King of Hexi, as Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies with staff, Commander of Liangzhou and all military affairs of the Western Regions and Qiang and Rong, Acting General Who Conquers the West, Grand Tutor, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Liang.
idiomatic: On renhai Li Shun, Concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies, was sent with credentials to invest Juqu Mengxun as King of Liang with full western command.

literal: On renshen an edict said: "Recently rebels have run wild; midsummer is not yet calm; war-chariots have been driven again and again without leisure to rest.
idiomatic: On renshen an edict declared: "Rebels have lately run wild; midsummer is not yet calm; the army has marched again and again without rest."

literal: Now the two foes are destroyed and troops and horses are at ease; we shall lay down arms and cultivate letters, follow the transformation of great peace, put neglected offices in order, raise reclusive men, lift up the obscure and poor, advance the eminent and able, and at dawn seek and think—longing to meet teachers and aides—as the Yin house's dream of the plank road could not surpass this.
idiomatic: Now both enemies are gone and the host is idle; we will sheathe arms, restore civil order, revive abandoned posts, call out the hidden, and seek worthy counselors from dawn—surpassing even the Yin king's dream of worthy men in the wild."

literal: Inquiry was made of all offices; all praised Fan Yang Lu Xuan, Boling Cui Chuo, Zhao commandery Li Ling, Hejian Xing Ying, Bohai Gao Yun, Guangping You Ya, Taiyuan Zhang Wei, and others—all eminent scions and the ornament of their provinces, fit for ceremonial display.
idiomatic: All offices named Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Cui Chuo of Boling, Li Ling of Zhao, Xing Ying of Hejian, Gao Yun of Bohai, You Ya of Guangping, Zhang Wei of Taiyuan, and others—men of talent and standing in their commands."

literal: Does the Odes not say, 'The crane cries from the deep marsh, its voice heard in heaven'? We hope to obtain such men, employ them in government, and together reach the beauty of universal harmony.
idiomatic: As the Odes says, 'The crane cries from the nine marshes, its voice heard in heaven'—may we find such men for office and share in ordered peace."

literal: The Changes says: 'I have fine rank; I will tie it to you.
idiomatic: The Changes says, 'I have fine rank; I will bind it to you.'"

literal: ' Men like Xuan who hide in their lanes and do not display their fame—all provinces and commanderies are to send them forth with ceremony.
idiomatic: Men like Xuan who live obscure without seeking fame—every province and commandery shall summon them with full ritual."

literal: " Xuan and the others and those sent by the provinces arrived—several hundred in all—and were appointed in due order.
idiomatic: Xuan and the rest, with those the provinces sent—several hundred in all—were ranked and appointed."

literal: Winter, tenth month, day wuyin: an edict that Chancellor Cui Hao was to revise the laws and ordinances.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on wuyin, he ordered Chancellor Cui Hao to revise the laws.

literal: Traveled to the southern desert.
idiomatic: He went to the southern desert.

literal: Eleventh month, day bingchen: Mo Fu Kuruyu of the northern Tiele led his tribe, tens of thousands of horse, driving several million deer to the imperial halt; the Emperor therefore held a great hunt to reward the followers, inscribed a stone in the southern desert, and recorded the merit.
idiomatic: On bingchen of the eleventh month Kuruyu, Mo Fu of the northern Tiele, brought tens of thousands of horse and millions of deer to the camp; the emperor held a great hunt for his followers and set up a stone in the desert to record the deed.

literal: Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin was demoted to duke for an offense.
idiomatic: Xi Jin, Prince of Yicheng, was reduced to duke for an offense.

literal: Twelfth month, day dingchou: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On dingchou of the twelfth month the court returned to the capital.

literal: Yanhe year 1, spring, first month, day bingwu: the Guardian Empress was honored as Empress Dowager; Lady Helian was made empress; Prince Huang was made crown prince; the ancestral temple was visited; general amnesty; the era was changed.
idiomatic: In the first year of Yanhe, first month of spring, on bingwu the Guardian Empress became Empress Dowager, Lady Helian empress, Prince Huang crown prince; the temple was visited, amnesty granted, and the reign title changed.

literal: On jisi an edict said: "With my slight person I have received the ancestral temple, thinking to expand the great foundation and clear the nine domains.
idiomatic: On jisi an edict said: "With this slight person I have received the ancestral shrine, intent on broadening the foundation and pacifying the realm."

literal: We met a declining age and the realm split apart.
idiomatic: We met a declining age and the empire fell apart."

literal: Therefore campaigns were repeated without rest; from Shiguang to now, in nine years the war-chariot has gone forth ten times.
idiomatic: Campaigns followed without pause—from Shiguang until now, in nine years the army marched ten times."

literal: Commanders civil and military bore spears and armor, combed wind and washed rain, trod blades, and shared toil with Us.
idiomatic: Generals and ministers bore arms, braved wind and rain, walked among blades, and shared our labor."

literal: Relying on the spirits' aid and the officers' and soldiers' exertion, We were able to break the strong and cut down the great foe.
idiomatic: By the spirits' help and the troops' strength we broke the strong and destroyed the great enemy."

literal: Arms did not reach their utmost and both foes were destroyed;
idiomatic: Arms were not pushed to excess, yet both enemies perished;"

literal: the army did not violate discipline and distant regions were at peace.
idiomatic: the army kept discipline and distant lands were calm."

literal: Moreover the seasons were harmonious and auspicious omens came down together throughout the commanderies and districts beyond counting—how could We alone receive this blessing? It is also what the ministers achieved in concert.
idiomatic: Seasons were mild and good omens beyond count filled the commands—could We alone deserve this? It came from the ministers acting as one."

literal: The dukes and ministers therefore, aligning with the meeting of Heaven and man, requested establishment of the heir.
idiomatic: The dukes and ministers, reading Heaven and man together, asked that the heir be set."

literal: The practice of reward and favor is to exalt old merit, display the able, and secure endless blessing; princes, dukes, generals, and all below were broadly raised in noble rank, founded states and inherited houses, restored abolished offices, raised eminent recluses, remitted burdensome levies, revised statutes, strove for lightness and simplicity, abolished the old and established the new, and rectified unity.
idiomatic: Rewards should honor past service and display talent for lasting peace; princes, dukes, generals, and all below were raised in rank, states founded, offices restored, the worthy called out, harsh taxes cut, laws revised for simplicity, the old replaced and unity set right."

literal: All offices should deeply consider effecting merit, keep to the straight way and correct the person, establish achievement and affairs, and not slacken—fitting Our intent."
idiomatic: Every office must seek real achievement, walk uprightly, build lasting work, and not slacken—so We intend."

literal: Second month, day bingzi: traveled to the Southern Palace.
idiomatic: On bingzi of the second month he went to the Southern Palace.

literal: Third month, day dingwei: Lady He was posthumously honored as empress.
idiomatic: On dingwei of the third month Lady He was posthumously made empress.

literal: On renshen Murong Mugui, King of Western Qin, sent Helian Ding to the capital.
idiomatic: On renshen Mugui, King of Western Qin, sent Helian Ding to the capital.

literal: Summer, fifth month: a great review of chariots and conscripts was held at the southern suburb, intending to campaign against Feng Wentong.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer the army was reviewed at the southern suburb to strike Feng Wentong.

literal: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Sixth month, day gengyin: the imperial carriage campaigned against Helong.
idiomatic: On gengyin of the sixth month the court marched on Helong.

literal: An edict that Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing An Yuan and others were to encamp in the southern desert against the Rouran.
idiomatic: He ordered An Yuan, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and others to camp in the southern desert against the Rouran.

literal: On xinmao Concurrent Attendant Cadet Deng Ying was envoy to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: On xinmao Deng Ying, Concurrent Attendant Cadet, went to Liu Yilong as envoy.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jiwei: the imperial carriage reached the Ru River.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiwei, the court reached the Ru River.

literal: On gengshen an edict that General Who Pacifies the East, Duke of Yicheng Xi Jin, was to mobilize the people of You province and more than ten thousand Dingling of Miyun, transport siege engines, and go by the southern route to join at Helong.
idiomatic: On gengshen he ordered Xi Jin, General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Yicheng, to raise the people of You and more than ten thousand Miyun Dingling with siege gear by the southern road to Helong.

literal: The Emperor reached Liaoxi; Wentong sent his attendant censor Cui Pin with cattle and wine as tribute.
idiomatic: Reaching Liaoxi, Wentong sent Cui Pin with cattle and wine.

literal: On jisi the imperial carriage reached Helong and came before the city.
idiomatic: On jisi the court reached Helong and stood before the walls.

literal: Li Chong, Administrator of Shicheng, Wang Rong, Administrator of Jiande, and more than ten commanderies came over; their people, thirty thousand, were set to dig encircling trenches for the siege.
idiomatic: Li Chong of Shicheng, Wang Rong of Jiande, and more than ten districts submitted; thirty thousand of their people dug siege trenches.

literal: That month the Eastern Palace was built.
idiomatic: That month the Eastern Palace was built.

literal: Eighth month, day jiaxu: Wentong sent tens of thousands of men out to challenge battle; Yuan Qiu of Changli and Yuan Qi of Hejian routed them; more than ten thousand died.
idiomatic: On jiaxu of the eighth month Wentong sent tens of thousands to fight; Yuan Qiu and Yuan Qi broke them and killed more than ten thousand.

literal: Gao Shao, Wentong's Master of Writing, led more than ten thousand households to hold the Qiang-Hu fort.
idiomatic: Gao Shao, Wentong's Master of Writing, held a Qiang-Hu fort with more than ten thousand households.

literal: On jimao the imperial carriage attacked Shao; on xinsi he was beheaded.
idiomatic: On jimao the court attacked Shao; on xinsi he was beheaded.

literal: An edict that General Who Pacifies the East He Duoluo was to attack Wentong's Administrator of Daifang Murong Xuan at Hou Fort; Grand General Who Inspires Awe, Prince of Yongchang Jian, was to attack Jiande; General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Leping Pi, was to attack Jiyang—all were taken, captives seized, and the generals rewarded each according to merit.
idiomatic: He Duoluo took Murong Xuan at Hou Fort; Prince Jian of Yongchang took Jiande; Prince Pi of Leping took Jiyang; captives were divided among the troops by merit.

literal: Ninth month, day yimao: the imperial carriage returned west.
idiomatic: On yimao of the ninth month the court turned west.

literal: The people of Yingqiu, Chengzhou, Liaodong, Lelang, Daifang, and Xuantu—thirty thousand households—were moved to You province; granaries were opened for relief.
idiomatic: Thirty thousand households from six northeastern commands were moved to You; granaries were opened for relief.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day guiyou: the imperial carriage reached the Ru River.
idiomatic: On guiyou of the tenth month of winter the court reached the Ru River.

literal: Murong Mugui of Tuyuhun sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Murong Mugui sent tribute.

literal: Eleventh month, day yisi: the imperial carriage returned from the campaign against Helong.
idiomatic: On yisi of the eleventh month the court returned from Helong.

literal: Twelfth month, day jichou: Feng Chong, Duke of Changle, and his mother and younger brother Lang, and Lang's younger brother Miao, submitted Liaoxi.
idiomatic: On jichou Feng Chong of Changle, his mother, Lang, and Miao brought Liaoxi over.

literal: Wentong sent the general Feng Yu to besiege Liaoxi.
idiomatic: Wentong sent Feng Yu to besiege Liaoxi.

literal: Earlier, worthies had been summoned, but provinces and commanderies often forced them to come.
idiomatic: Earlier worthies had been summoned, but local officials often forced them out.

literal: An edict said: "We have removed the false and pacified violence, campaigning for years, seeking worthy men to illumine government; therefore provinces and commanderies were ordered to search out the hidden and advance the able.
idiomatic: An edict said: "We have fought for years seeking able men to govern; provinces were told to find the hidden and promote talent."

literal: The gentlemen of old nurtured their will behind closed gates; when virtue was complete and work achieved, their talent served the age.
idiomatic: Men of old kept their will at home; when ready, they served the state."

literal: Some came with easy grace only after three summons;
idiomatic: Some came slowly, only after repeated calls;"

literal: some hurried in haste, carrying the cauldron to present themselves.
idiomatic: others hurried forward bearing the cauldron themselves."

literal: Though their paths differed, the aim of aiding the time was one.
idiomatic: Different paths served the same end."

literal: All summoned men are to be instructed with ceremony and allowed to come or go as they choose—why force them?
idiomatic: Every summoned man shall be told with full courtesy and left free to come or go—why compel them?"

literal: These governors and magistrates have failed to proclaim Our intent; they bring no added light but only display Our want of virtue.
idiomatic: These governors have misrepresented Our intent and shown Our lack of virtue rather than Our praise."

literal: From now on let village and district recommend; magistrates need only declare Our sincere search for the worthy.
idiomatic: Henceforth let communities recommend; officials need only announce Our search for talent."

literal: When they arrive they shall receive exceptional promotion; according to civil or martial talent they shall be placed in government.
idiomatic: On arrival they shall be raised without waiting for routine rank and set to civil or military office as fit."

literal: Proclaim this edict clearly so all may hear."
idiomatic: Let this edict be proclaimed until all have heard."

literal: That year Tufa Rutan's son Baozhou abandoned Juqu Mengxun and came in flight; Baozhou was made Duke of Zhangye.
idiomatic: That year Baozhou, son of Tufa Rutan, fled from Juqu Mengxun and was made Duke of Zhangye.

literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day yimao: Grand General Who Inspires Awe, Prince of Yongchang Jian, directed the armies to relieve Liaoxi.
idiomatic: In the second year, first month of spring, on yimao Prince Jian of Yongchang led the armies to save Liaoxi.

literal: On bingyin Prince of Le'an Fan was made Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies with staff, Commander of Qin, Yong, Jing, Liang, and Yi provinces, General of the Guard with equal ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and garrisoned Chang'an.
idiomatic: On bingyin Fan, Prince of Le'an, was given western command and garrisoned Chang'an.

literal: Second month, day gengwu: an edict that Concurrent Director of Ceremonial Affairs Li Ji, bearing credentials, was to make Feng Chong Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and King of Liaoxi, with authority to appoint offices through the Masters of Writing;
idiomatic: On gengwu Li Ji was sent to invest Feng Chong as King of Liaoxi with power to staff his court;

literal: Chong and his meritorious followers were enfeoffed and ranked each according to merit.
idiomatic: Chong and his followers were enfeoffed by merit.

literal: General Who Conquers the West Jin Ya and Yanpu, garrison commander of Anding, and Governor of Jingzhou Di Ziyu contended for power and raised troops against Yanpu; they did not prevail, withdrew to hold Hukong Valley, drove off civilians, and entrenched on difficult ground.
idiomatic: Jin Ya, General Who Conquers the West, quarreled with Yanpu of Anding and Di Ziyu of Jing; failing to win, they held Hukong Valley, looted civilians, and fortified the heights.

literal: An edict that Attendant Cadet, General Who Pacifies the West, and garrison commander of Anding Lu Si was to campaign and capture them.
idiomatic: He ordered Lu Si, Attendant Cadet and commander of Anding, to take them.

literal: On renwu traveled to Hexi.
idiomatic: On renwu he went to Hexi.

literal: An edict that Concurrent Attendant Cadet Song Xuan was envoy to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: He ordered Song Xuan, Concurrent Attendant Cadet, to Liu Yilong.

literal: On bingshen Feng Chong's younger brother Lang came to court.
idiomatic: On bingshen Lang, Feng Chong's brother, came to court.

literal: Third month: Tian Zhu, son of Sima Yuanxian, Grand General of Agile Cavalry to Sima Dezong, came over.
idiomatic: In the third month Tian Zhu, son of Sima Yuanxian, came over from the Jin court.

literal: On renzi the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On renzi the court returned to the capital.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day jihai: traveled to north of the mountains.
idiomatic: On jihai of the fifth month of summer he went north of the mountains.

literal: Sixth month: Grand General Who Inspires Awe, Prince of Yongchang Jian, and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing An Yuan directed the armies to campaign against Helong.
idiomatic: In the sixth month Prince Jian of Yongchang and An Yuan led the armies against Helong.
